slowest_experiments.title: Runtime constraint instrumentation
slowest_experiments.root_cause: Massive outlier — likely an iterative debugging loop where constraint instrumentation failed silently and required multiple retries. No timeout guard or structured diagnostic path; the session spiraled into ad-hoc investigation rather than a bound-and-escalate pattern.

slowest_experiments.title: Live GSM8K semantic benchmark on Qwen3.5-0.8B and Gemma
slowest_experiments.root_cause: Sequential two-model live inference over a large question set (50+ questions) with both models loaded serially. GPU 1 sat idle while GPU 0 ran Qwen, then GPU 0 sat idle while GPU 1 ran Gemma. DualGPURunner pattern was not yet in place at this point in the milestone.

slowest_experiments.title: 3B model verification — does verify-repair help large models
slowest_experiments.root_cause: Large 3B model (full context window) inference with binary verify-repair applied indiscriminately. False-positive repair gating (later fixed in confidence_verifier.py) caused repair loops to run on correct answers, consuming extra tokens and time. Root cause identified and resolved post-milestone.

slowest_experiments.title: Live prompt-side constraint benchmark on typed IR tasks
slowest_experiments.root_cause: Live prompt-side benchmarks require full model forward passes per question. Like Exp 219, no batching (8-16 questions/pass) was in place — each question triggered a separate model call, inflating latency by 4-8x vs. batched inference. BatchedInferenceRunner introduced in Exp 306.

slowest_experiments.title: Retrain JEPA violation predictor v2 with multi-domain data
slowest_experiments.root_cause: Multi-domain JEPA training with no checkpoint resume path — if the session was interrupted or encountered an error mid-training, the entire run restarted from scratch. Checkpoint-resume pattern (atomic save/load) was standardized only in the experiment template (Exp 306).

gpu_utilization_analysis.detail: GPUs were used one at a time for the bulk of the milestone. Two-model experiments (Exp 219, 221, 235, 258) loaded models sequentially, leaving the idle GPU unused. DualGPURunner was wired into experiments starting ~Exp 282, covering the final ~50 experiments. Estimated 280 of 330 experiments ran with only one GPU active.
gpu_utilization_analysis.zombie_detail: gpu_monitor.py --kill-zombies detected no true zombies (no process held >1GB VRAM idle >10 min). The 2MB allocations visible at retro time are CUDA context stubs, not zombie workloads.

bottlenecks_identified: SEQUENTIAL GPU EXECUTION: ~280/330 experiments ran on a single GPU while the second RTX 3090 (24GB) sat idle. Two-model comparisons (Qwen vs. Gemma) loaded models one-at-a-time instead of in parallel via DualGPURunner.

UNBATCHED INFERENCE: Single-question forward passes dominated live-GPU experiments. Questions were processed one-at-a-time rather than in batches of 8-16, wasting 4-8x GPU throughput on prompt-processing overhead.

NO TIMEOUT GUARD ON EXP 53: A single experiment (Exp 53, runtime constraint instrumentation) consumed 418 minutes — 9.4% of the entire milestone wall time. There was no structured escalation path for failed debugging sessions.

MISSING CHECKPOINT RESUME IN EARLY EXPERIMENTS: Training and long inference runs (Exps 155, 184) had no atomic checkpoint-save/resume. An interruption meant full restart, doubling or tripling wall time.

FALSE-POSITIVE REPAIR LOOPS: Exp 184 and related verify-repair experiments wasted inference tokens repairing already-correct answers. Binary gating (repair on any violation) was not replaced with confidence-weighted gating until late in the milestone.

COLD-START BOILERPLATE PER EXPERIMENT: Each experiment script replicated ~150 lines of setup (directory creation, checkpoint loading, GPU pre-warm, artifact schema). No shared template until Exp 306 (final 1% of the milestone).

DOC RECONCILIATION LATENCY: ops/status.md, ops/changelog.md, and traceability.md were updated inline at the end of each experiment turn. For short experiments, this overhead was proportionally large (30-40% of turn time).
PREFLIGHT TEST SUITE GROWTH: The pytest suite grew from ~2800 to ~3975 tests over the milestone. Full-suite runs at each turn added ~15-20s overhead per experiment — manageable but growing.
improvements_suggested: DUAL-GPU PARALLELISM BY DEFAULT: Wire DualGPURunner into ExperimentTemplate.setup_gpu() so all new experiments get parallel model loading for free. Target: both GPUs above 40% utilization for two-model experiments. Estimated saving: 10-15% of milestone wall time.

MANDATORY BATCHED INFERENCE: BatchedInferenceRunner (Exp 306) is now available — make it the only supported inference path in ExperimentTemplate. Batch size 8-16, timeout = batch_size * 60s. Estimated saving: 8-12% for GPU-heavy experiments.

HARD TIME-BOX WITH AUTO-ESCALATE: Any single experiment exceeding 45 minutes should auto-checkpoint and surface a structured blocker artifact (status='timeout_escalate') rather than continuing to spiral. Conductor should detect >45min sessions and prompt user. Estimated saving: eliminates Exp 53-class outliers, ~5-8% of milestone wall time.

ATOMIC CHECKPOINT RESUME FOR ALL TRAINING RUNS: Checkpoint-save (atomic write) every 10% of training steps, with resume detection at startup. Already standardized in ExperimentTemplate; back-apply the pattern to any remaining training scripts (JEPA retrain, EBM training). Estimated saving: 4-6% for training experiments.

CONFIDENCE-WEIGHTED REPAIR GATING EVERYWHERE: Replace binary verify-repair with ConfidenceVerifier.verify_with_confidence(threshold=0.8) in all pipeline experiments. Prevents false-positive repair loops from inflating per-experiment time. Estimated saving: 3-5%.

LAZY DOC UPDATES — BATCH AT MILESTONE BOUNDARY: Defer per-experiment doc reconciliation (changelog, status, traceability) to a single batched pass every 5 experiments or at natural session boundaries. Reduces doc-update overhead from ~35% to ~10% of short experiment turns. Estimated saving: 3-4%.

GPU_MONITOR INTEGRATION IN CONDUCTOR: Run gpu_monitor.py --json before each experiment and inject the report into the conductor prompt. The conductor can then auto-select DualGPURunner vs. single-GPU path and warn on zombie processes before they accumulate.
EXPERIMENT TEMPLATE ADOPTION METRIC: Track what fraction of new experiments use ExperimentTemplate. Target ≥90% by mid-milestone. Report the metric in ops/metrics.md each session.

PREFLIGHT TEST PARALLELISM: Split the ~4000-test suite into two workers (pytest-xdist -n 2). Given the current sequential single-core run, this halves preflight overhead from ~20s to ~10s with no code changes.

estimated_time_savings_detail.note: Additive estimates sum to 38% but improvements overlap (e.g. DualGPU + batching both reduce inference time). Realistic combined estimate is 28%, equivalent to saving ~1240 minutes on an equivalent 4430-minute milestone.
